title: Tying off cleanly
subtitle: How to end a thread on the back without a knot or a visible tail.
excerpt: Ending thread cleanly means running the tail under worked stitches on the back and trimming flush. No knot is needed. A knot on the back bulks through the front and can work loose in washing.
sourceNotes:
Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776. Thread ending and finishing methods.
Weldon's Practical Needlework, volume 1 (1886), Internet Archive. Finishing thread on the back of counted work.

glossaryTerms.definition: The short end of thread left after ending a working length. The tail is secured by running it under existing stitches on the back of the cloth, then trimmed flush.

content.text: When a working thread runs low, about 10 cm left on the needle, end it on the back of the cloth. The
is secured under existing stitches and then trimmed flush. A knot is never placed on the back of a finished piece.
When about 10 cm of thread remains on the needle, make the last stitch and bring the needle to the back of the cloth.
Slide the needle under the back of three or four already-worked stitches in the same colour area. Pull the thread through slowly.
If the colour area is small, run the tail diagonally under stitches in more than one direction to prevent it from working loose.
Hold the cloth flat and trim the tail flush with the surface of the back using embroidery scissors. Cut as close to the cloth as possible without snipping an existing stitch.
Do not carry the tail across an unstitched area on the back. The dark thread will show through pale fabric and the loose tail can snag as later stitches are worked.

attrs.heading: What goes wrong
attrs.intro: Three problems with endings that affect the finished look.

items.symptom: A small loop or tail appears on the front
items.cause: The tail was trimmed at an angle that left a tiny loop catching on the front surface.
items.fix: Trim with the scissors parallel to the cloth surface, not at an angle. Small scissors with fine points help on crowded areas.

items.symptom: A thread tail works loose after washing
items.cause: Only one or two stitches were used to secure the tail.
items.fix: Always run under at least three stitches, and ideally four. On slippery threads such as silk, run under six stitches or pass the needle back on itself to lock the tail.

items.symptom: A dark tail shows through light fabric
items.cause: The tail was carried across an unstitched background area on the back.
items.fix: End the thread at the last stitch of one colour section, then start a new thread when you reach the next section. Carrying a thread more than two or three holes risks show-through.

content.text: Clean ending is as important as clean starting for a professional-looking back. The same technique applies to surface embroidery, Hardanger, and Sashiko.
also reduces the bulk on the back that causes lumps when a piece is pressed or mounted.
